root.claim: One deterministic fixed-tape Turing machine computes the exact $2n$-bit product of two $n$-bit integers in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time with $\kappa=2^{-182}$.
root.method: build two linear-network tape procedures, fast address interchange and simultaneous butterfly layers, from fixed networks with a strict rank saving; use them in synthetic transforms; place these in the Harvey–van der Hoeven reduction through radix digits, a CRT map, Gaussian resampling with retained permutations, Bluestein chirps and a phase twist; and bound every cost term

motivation.text: A single scan per transform level already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$, so going below $n\log n$ needs savings in both address movement and butterfly arithmetic.

quote.quote:
Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of
$\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.
We therefore need savings in both movement and arithmetic.

root.salient: The exponent saving $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is tiny but fixed, so the cost is $o(n\log n)$ through all input lengths, refuting the Schönhage–Strassen conjecture in this model.

adds.name: stored bit volume
adds.meaning: The number of data bits in the array a tape procedure operates on.

adds.name: working precision
adds.meaning: The number of fractional bits $6\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$ of the fixed-point grid.

children.claim: On a fixed number of tapes, digit moves, permutations of two digit values, splits with fixed pointwise maps, cyclic row splits, controlled shifts and fixed rational scalings of an address field each cost $O(V)$ on an array of volume $V$.
children.method: stream each operation in lexicographic address order, splitting the array into a fixed number of aligned streams and merging them back

motivation.text: Addresses are implicit in the position of an entry in the ordered stream, so any operation that needs only a fixed number of aligned streams, or a target field that follows its controls, can be done in a bounded number of scans.

children.claim: Fixed digit-pair permutations, single-digit moves, splits with a pointwise map, and cyclic splits of whole rows into $W$ streams each cost $O(V)$.

quote.quote:

fixed number of control values.

children.claim: Two fixed linear networks, a bit network over $\mathbb F_2$ and a complex network over $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$, exchange two data banks while restoring every scratch value, and the total number $s$ of smaller operations their frame changes need is strictly below $Wm$, with $s/W<m^{1-2^{-50}}$.
children.method: build a three-stage bank-exchange network on three-element subsets of a 100-element set, carry arrays through it in frames that commute with the gates, label vertices by nested nondegenerate subspaces whose residual dimensions count the smaller calls, and check both interfaces and the explicit deficits

motivation.text: A strict deficit $s<Wm$ means that multiplying the recursion parameter by $m$ multiplies the per-bit recursive cost by $s/W<m$, which is what yields a power saving.

quote.quote:
This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

children.salient: The deficit is minute (relative deficit near $10^{-11}$) yet strict, and the same triple-subset design achieves it over two different scalar domains.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial scratch values, a forward invocation at stage 1, an inverse invocation at stage 2 and a forward invocation at stage 3 send $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$ and restore every auxiliary value.
children.method: run an eight-row schedule per invocation that first subtracts the effect of the old scratch values, then copies, gathers, scatters and injects to add $x$ to $y$, then restores the scratch; compose three such invocations

motivation.text: Subtracting the scratch contribution before adding the source contribution, and undoing copy and gather afterwards, makes the net change independent of whatever the scratch wires held.

quote.quote:
The first two rows of
the following schedule remove the effect of the old scratch values;
the next four introduce the source values and add their effect to the
target; the last two restore the scratch values.

children.salient: The exchange works for arbitrary, unknown initial scratch values, which all come back unchanged.
